neighbours.label: ' he' opening a generic 'he that …' relative clause in scripture-style aphorisms (the model expects 'that/which' next)
fire: Hear now this saying, and remember it: he that walketh uprightly walketh surely.
Verily, verily, I say unto thee, he that keepeth the law shall be blessed.
Woe unto the proud; but he that humbleth himself shall be exalted.
Mark well the word of the prophet: he that soweth iniquity shall reap vanity.
Thus saith the Lord unto his servants, he that overcometh shall inherit all things.
The wise man spake thus: he that spareth his rod hateth his son.
Therefore take heed, my brethren, for he that endureth unto the end shall be saved.
Again I tell you plainly, he that is faithful in little is faithful also in much.
quiet: Hear now this story of the shepherd: in the morning he walked with his flock.
Verily, when the night came, he lay down beside the well and slept.
Woe came upon the city, and he fled with his household into the hills.
Mark the prophet as he came down from the mountain with the tablets.
Thus the servant departed, and he returned to his master at evening.
The wise man rose early, and he went out into the field to pray.
Therefore the king was wroth, and he sent his captains against the city.
Again the people murmured, and he spake unto them of the bread from heaven.

notes: Card: top ' he' examples are KJV 'he that soweth', 'He that rejecteth'; Spanish 'el que' also appears but probed weakly. Logit: - pole promotes 'that/which'. Near misses are KJV-style narrative ' he' as plain subject.
